title: La Gritería
desc: December 7, and the shouting arrives at your door
setting: It is six in the evening on the seventh and fifteen children are already at your gate.

options.feedback: The one answer there is, and you had it ready. Nobody here will forget that you did.
You know what it is about, but the call has a fixed answer and this is not it.
A greeting where a response goes. The whole street will hear the gap.

options.es: Ya voy, ya voy. Traigo gofio y rosquillas.
options.en: Coming, coming. I have gofio and rosquillas.
options.feedback: The gorras are the little gifts handed out at the door, not hats. Naming what you are bringing is half the fun.
Fine, and they will wait. Naming what you are bringing is half the fun.
On the seventh of December this is the one sentence you cannot say at your own door.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.en: Ideay, there is sugar cane as well!

options.es: Uno para cada uno, no peleen.
options.feedback: Said like somebody who has done this before, which is the impression you want.
It works. Twelve children and no rule is how it all ends up with four of them.
There is no later. The next house is waiting for them.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.es: ¡Gracias! Ya nos vamos a la otra casa.
steps.en: Thank you! We are off to the next house.

options.en: Go carefully! And have a good night.
options.feedback: Sending them off with a word is what a neighbour does, and they are running to the next gate.
Correct Spanish, and flat for a doorway with fifteen children in it.
They were saying goodbye, not asking for more.
